structured_output.summary:
Phase 4 ("Management and shared modules") meets its acceptance criteria with independently verifiable evidence. All 93 phase-4-owned baseline operations (87 `management` family + 6 `iam`) are mapped in `contracts/native-operation-mappings/*.json` and implemented: 56 non-DLP management methods (profiles 9, topics 10, api keys 6, customer apps 6, deployment profiles 1, legacy DLP profiles 1, scan logs 1, dashboard 22), 24 canonical DLP methods, 2 token-administration methods, 5 OAuth provider lifecycle methods, and 6 IAM scope methods. `tools/native_operations.py --check --require-through-phase 4` mechanically rejects any owned operation lacking a `pub fn` and a named test, and it passed (99 implemented, 97 complete/2 deliberately partial Gateway representatives owned by Phase 6).

I verified wire fidelity by reading the frozen TypeScript (`.local/typescript/src/management/*`, `src/management/dlp/*`, `src/iam/scopes-client.ts`, `src/constants.ts`, `src/listing.ts`) against the Rust: routes, path constants (including the singular `/v1/mgmt/customerapp/tsg`), query spellings (`pageNumber`/`pageSize`, `appid`/`appname`, `tokenTtlInterval`), all eight dashboard query dialects and their Zod defaults (30/days, 1/day, 30+limit 25/offset 0, no-window scan content), the Spring `last` → `totalPages` → short-page stopping order with size 50, topic latest-revision grouping semantics (first-seen order, strict `>` ties), `next_offset || undefined` end detection, and IAM create/update/bind body construction. Everything matched, with each intentional divergence (stricter cursor/ID/multipart/query validation, explicit truncation, no mutation replay, Rust User-Agent) recorded both in docs and machine-readably in the mapping fragments.

Security posture is strong and tested, not asserted: validation and query/URL bounds run before any token request (`token.calls == 0`, `wire.requests == 0` assertions), every one of the 15 management, 12 DLP, 2 token and 4 IAM write paths is proven single-dispatch under `with_retries(5)` with `RemoteOutcome::Unknown`, `x-tsg-id` is derived only from immutable OAuth identity (forced on for dashboard/IAM, forced off for OAuth management), endpoint overrides are policy-checked (denied origin rejected locally), and Debug/Display redaction is asserted for cursors, rows, queries, tokens and upstream bodies. `multipart.rs` validates part names/filenames/MIME, rejects CRLF/quote/traversal injection, bounds the envelope, and scans all part bytes for the chosen boundary. `pagination.rs` is bounded on items/bytes/pages plus independent cursor-size/history limits, latches failures, detects repeated cursors and empty non-final pages, and shares one absolute deadline.

Check evidence is real, not prose: `docs/checks/phase-04.json` records 29 commands with actual stdout/stderr, `source_sha256` equal to the reviewed SHA, `source_unchanged: true`, including two toolchains (1.88.0/1.99.0) × nine feature sets on x86_64-unknown-linux-musl with fmt/clippy `-D warnings`/test/doc, 217 passing Rust tests under `--all-features`, package extraction and compilation, generation reproducibility, and the schema oracle. `docs/reviews/phase-04-pre-review-fixes.md` honestly records an earlier IAM-only clippy gate failure and its fix rather than hiding it.

Remaining issues are all minor: an unnecessary `management → iam` feature edge (which also makes a `#[cfg]` and a doc sentence vacuous), one undocumented header-inheritance behavior for DLP, order-insensitive query assertions in the management fixtures, two compressed one-liners, and an edge-case cursor-limit data-loss path unreachable with phase-4's u64 cursors. None block advancement; live acceptance remains explicitly deferred to Phase 8 and is not a phase-4 criterion.

findings.description: `management = ["models", "dlp", "iam"]` makes the IAM client part of every management build although nothing under `crates/scm-sdk/src/airs/` references `iam` (verified by grep) and `ManagementClient` exposes no IAM convenience accessor. The same edge makes `#[cfg(feature = "dlp")]` on `ManagementClient::dlp` (src/airs/management/mod.rs:109) vacuous and makes docs/MANAGEMENT.md:11 ("requires ... the `dlp` feature") misleading, since `dlp` can never be absent when `management` is on.
findings.required_fix: Either drop `iam` from the `management` feature (keeping `dlp` because `ManagementClient::dlp` needs it) or add the intended management→IAM convenience accessor; then correct docs/MANAGEMENT.md:11 to state that `management` always enables DLP.

findings.description: DLP.md states the client "retains the caller's transport, destination admission, tenant identity, request bounds and session" but never says that DLP requests inherit the caller's `x-tsg-id` setting. The frozen `DlpNamespace` (src/management/client.ts:107) is constructed without `tsgId` and therefore never sends that header, whereas crates/scm-sdk/tests/dlp_contracts.rs:111 builds the fixture client with the tenant header enabled and asserts `x-tsg-id` on every DLP request, so the fixtures read as if the header were part of the DLP contract.
findings.required_fix: Document in docs/DLP.md that the tenant header is caller-selected (as docs/MANAGEMENT.md:13 and docs/FOUNDATION.md:169 do) and that the frozen baseline sends none to the DLP service, and/or add a DLP fixture case built with the header disabled to pin both behaviours.

findings.description: Management fixtures compare query parameters as a `BTreeMap` (plus a duplicate-key count check), so query ordering is not asserted. This is why the same `sessions_overview` operation is expected as [time_interval, time_unit, limit, offset] at line 762 and as [time_interval, time_unit, offset, limit] at line 1641 without failing. The DLP fixtures do assert ordered pairs (tests/dlp_contracts.rs:163), so the documented "retain the source's query dialects" claim for the 22 dashboard methods is verified only as a key/value set.
findings.required_fix: Assert the ordered query pair vector for the dashboard identity/page/window queries (as dlp_contracts.rs does), or state explicitly in docs/MANAGEMENT.md that only the query key/value set, not the emission order, is a verified contract.

findings.description: `nonblank` is a single >200-character line combining the whitespace class, trim and branch; crates/scm-sdk/src/airs/management/dashboard.rs:144 similarly packs a Debug-impl macro onto one line. Both pass `cargo fmt --check` but are markedly harder to read and audit than the rest of the crate, and the whitespace set in `nonblank` is security-relevant (it gates topic force-delete audit identity).
findings.required_fix: Expand both to normal multi-line form, and give the whitespace class a named constant so the trim set can be reviewed against the frozen `updatedBy.trim()` semantics at a glance.

findings.description: When a fetched page carries an oversized `next` cursor, the walk fails before `pages_read += 1`, so the rows already received and bounded on that page are discarded and the saved resume position points at the page that just failed (pagination/tests.rs:465 pins this: `error.partial().items.is_empty()` with `resume.cursor == "small"`). Resuming therefore fails deterministically at the same point, and product clients construct `Pages::new` with default cursor limits and expose no override. Not reachable in phase-4 scope, where every product cursor is `u64`, but it becomes reachable for opaque/string cursors in later families.
findings.required_fix: Either retain the accepted rows of the page whose next cursor was rejected (advancing `pages_read` and returning them in `partial()`), or document in docs/PAGINATION.md that an oversized returned cursor discards that page and requires explicitly raised `CursorLimits` to make progress, and plan a per-client cursor-limit override before the first non-u64 cursor family.
